listen.description: Socket address for the HTTP listener. Deploy a TLS-terminating reverse proxy in front of this address.

metrics_listen.description: Socket address for the Prometheus `/metrics` listener. Leave unset to disable the metrics listener.

public_url.description: External browser origin of the service: scheme, lowercase host, and optional non-default port, with no path or trailing slash. Used to validate the `Origin` header on state-changing requests and to construct the OIDC redirect URI.

cookie_secure.description: Whether session and login cookies set the `Secure` attribute and `__Host-` prefix. Set to `false` only for local plain-HTTP testing.

database.description: Absolute path to the SQLite database file. The controller holds an exclusive file lock on this path while running.

session_lifetime.description: Maximum lifetime of a browser session before the user must sign in again.

session_idle.description: Maximum idle time between requests for a browser session. Must not exceed `session_lifetime`.

key_lifetime.description: Validity period of a device's WireGuard public key after it is set or renewed, at least 4 days. When a key expires, the reconciler removes the peer from the kernel until a key is set again.

interfaces.description: Managed WireGuard interfaces keyed by Linux interface name (which also serves as the interface ID in the API).

Oidc.description: OpenID Connect relying-party settings for browser sign-in.

client_id.description: OAuth 2.0 client ID for browser sign-in.

secret_file.description: Absolute path to the file containing the OIDC client secret. Re-read on each use so secret rotation does not require a restart.

admin_groups.description: Group names in the ID token's `groups` claim that grant administrator privileges for the session.

Scim.description: Optional SCIM 2.0 user status polling. When configured, the controller checks user status at sign-in and periodically on `interval`, revoking sessions and device keys when an account is disabled or deleted at the identity provider.

url.description: Base URL of the SCIM 2.0 service.

client_id.description: OAuth 2.0 client ID used for client-credentials token requests to the SCIM API.

secret_file.description: Absolute path to the file containing the SCIM client secret.

health_subject.description: SCIM User ID of a canary account that remains permanently enabled. Before acting on a negative lookup result (disabled or 404), the controller verifies that this canary user is still reported as active, preventing upstream directory outages from mass-revoking accounts.

interval.description: Interval between background SCIM status sweeps across all accounts.

Interface.description: WireGuard interface configuration, address pools, and client configuration hints.

private_key_file.description: Absolute path to the server's WireGuard private key file (as generated by `wg genkey`). Read once at startup.

listen_port.description: UDP port the server interface listens on.

endpoint.description: External `host:port` endpoint that clients connect to.

addresses.description: CIDR addresses assigned to the server interface, such as `10.0.0.1/24`.

disabled.description: When `true`, the reconciler brings the interface down and removes all peers.

client_mtu.description: Suggested MTU for client configs, or `0` to let the client choose automatically.

dns.description: DNS server IP addresses included in client configs.

dns_search.description: DNS search domains included in client configs.

dns_zone.description: Authoritative DNS zone served by `[dns]` for devices on this interface, or empty to disable. Multiple interfaces can share a zone. Also appended to the client's DNS search domains after `dns_search`.

keepalive.description: PersistentKeepalive interval in seconds for client configs, or `0` to disable.

default_profile_id.description: ID of the default route profile for clients, or empty when `route_profiles` is empty.

route_profiles.description: Named sets of client-side `AllowedIPs` that users can choose between.

pools.description: Address pools from which device addresses and prefix grants are allocated.

RouteProfile.description: Named set of `AllowedIPs` that a client can select for its local tunnel routes. Selecting a profile changes only the client's `AllowedIPs`, leaving the server's peer routes unchanged.

id.description: Profile identifier: a DNS label that is unique within the interface.

name.description: Display name shown to users in the portal and agent UI.

allowed_ips.description: Client-side `AllowedIPs` prefixes routed through the tunnel when this profile is active.

Pool.description: Address pool from which device addresses and routed prefixes are allocated.

prefix.description: CIDR prefix of the pool, such as `10.0.0.0/24`. Pools must not overlap within or across interfaces.

min_prefix_length.description: Minimum prefix length (largest block size) a single grant from this pool may have. When unset, only single-host grants (`/32` or `/128`) are allowed.

max_prefixes.description: Maximum number of grants a single device may hold from this pool.

exclusions.description: Sub-prefixes inside the pool that are reserved and never allocated to devices.

Dns.description: Optional authoritative DNS server for interface `dns_zone` domains. Publishes `A` and `AAAA` records at `<dns_name>.<dns_zone>` for each device that has a `dns_name`.

listen.description: UDP and TCP socket address for the authoritative DNS listener.

name_server.description: Authoritative nameserver hostname placed in zone `NS` and `SOA` records. Must lie outside every configured `dns_zone` and resolve independently, because the server does not publish glue records.

ttl.description: Time to live in seconds for DNS records and negative caching responses.

DefaultQuota.description: Default per-account address limits. Each limit is a decimal address count (such as `"16"`), a CIDR prefix length (such as `"/64"`), or `""` for unlimited. Administrators can override these defaults on individual accounts.

ipv4.description: Default IPv4 address limit per account.

ipv6.description: Default IPv6 address limit per account.

level.description: Log filter directives in `tracing_subscriber::EnvFilter` syntax, such as `info` or `info,ito::reconcile=debug`.

requests.description: Whether to log every HTTP response at `info` level. Leave `false` when the reverse proxy already records access logs.

format.description: Output format: `auto` (systemd journal when stderr is connected to journald, otherwise plain text on stderr), `text` (plain text on stderr), or `json` (newline-delimited JSON on stderr).

oneOf.description: Native systemd journal when stderr is connected to journald, otherwise plain text.
